name: STEP
description: Spiking Transformers have recently emerged as promising architectures for combining the efficiency of spiking neural networks with the representational power of self-attention. However, the lack of standardized implementations, evaluation pipelines, and consistent design choices has hindered fair comparison and principled analysis. In this paper, we introduce STEP a unified benchmark framework for Spiking Transformers that supports a wide range of tasks, including classification, segmentation, and detection across static, event-based, and sequential datasets. STEP provides modular support for diverse components such as spiking neurons, input encodings, surrogate gradients, and multiple backends (e.g., SpikingJelly, BrainCog). Using STEP, we reproduce and evaluate several representative models, and conduct systematic ablation studies on attention design, neuron types, encoding schemes, and temporal modeling capabilities. We also propose a unified analytical model for energy estimation,
reputation: A new unified benchmark framework for Spiking Transformers that aims to standardize evaluation across tasks and implementations, but it is not yet a widely established community benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark spanning multiple modalities and tasks; scores are task-dependent and often reported alongside energy estimates and ablations rather than a single universal metric.
